A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CorrCLIP for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation, and their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 also includes Supplementary Material, which was inspected.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation evaluations across eight benchmarks, component ablations, parameter studies and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, correlation experiments and ablations, plus supplementary domain-generalization and computational results.

M1.justification: V2 adds feature refinement through lower-layer spatial features and mask class tokens, substantially changing feature computation (Section 3.4). Its appendix introduces faster variants that replace SAM and omit value reconstruction and mask merging. V1's plural-form class-name correction is no longer included in the described pipeline.

E1.justification: The eight original benchmarks remain. V2 additionally evaluates FoodSeg103, ATLANTIS, CUB-200 and SUIM from MESS (Table 9), extending coverage to food, waterbody, fine-grained bird and underwater segmentation domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparators including LaVG, NACLIP, Trident, ResCLIP, SC-CLIP, CLIPer, CASS, CAT-Seg and ESC-Net. SCLIP's ViT-L/14 and ViT-H/14 rows disappear, although its ViT-B/16 comparison remains. Supplementary Table 9 additionally compares against OVSeg-L and CAT-Seg-L.

E3.justification: The headline validation splits, mIoU metric and image-resizing/sliding-window settings remain. V2 introduces controlled inter-class interaction proportions, mask-resolution sweeps and computational comparisons using 8×8 versus 32×32 prompt grids. The CLIP-variant analysis also changes its aggregation from eight benchmarks in v1 Table 5 to five background-free benchmarks in v2 Table 7.

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled intra/inter-class correlation analyses, scope reconstruction applied to other methods, mask-resolution sensitivity, separate feature-branch ablations and component-level computational analysis. Conversely, v1's detailed SAM-threshold and DBSCAN-parameter sweeps are absent; mask merging is instead tested through an on/off comparison across several benchmarks.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. V2's added performance differences are point-score comparisons, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1's reported CorrCLIP averages change from 49.7 to 51.0 for ViT-B/16, 51.0 to 53.6 for ViT-L/14, and 50.0 to 52.3 for ViT-H/14. These concern revised CorrCLIP variants on the retained benchmarks, rather than unchanged-method reruns. V2 also supplies new domain-generalization, correlation, feature-refinement and efficiency results.

T1.justification: The interaction-matrix definition changes the unsegmented-region term from the broadcast sum of m0 and its transpose in v1 Equation (6) to their outer product in v2 Equation (7), changing the formal mask definition. V2 also introduces the weighted feature-refinement expression in Equation (11). Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes coherent correlations, outlier patches and similarity irregularity. V2 makes identifying inter-class correlations as the primary impediment a central contribution, and adds spatial/semantic feature refinement to its main claims. Class-name correction disappears from the contribution statements.

C2.justification: Value reconstruction is reinterpreted as suppressing residual inter-class correlations within imperfect masks, rather than chiefly correcting similarity irregularity after scope restriction. V2 adds substantive discussion of mixed-class masks, mask-downsampling errors, feature/text misalignment and computational bottlenecks, including explanations of branch-specific performance degradation and efficiency tradeoffs.

D1.justification: The core backbone choices, thresholds and sliding-window recipe remain. V2 adds a code-repository pointer, feature weights, the selected 42×42 mask resolution, CPU clustering information, RTX 4090/FP16 measurement conditions, and backbone/pretraining details for alternative mask generators. These extend the implementation documentation without replacing its existing core recipe.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands its treatment of recent OVSS approaches, distinguishing self-self attention, lower-layer attention refinement and external foundation-model methods. It positions explicit interaction-scope control against these approaches and adds literature supporting specialized-domain evaluation, fully supervised comparisons and alternative mask generators.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the inter-class correlation argument. Method exposition is reorganized into feature refinement and map correction, replacing the earlier combined correction subsection, and v2 adds a structured supplementary narrative. The title is also shortened and refocused.

P2.justification: V1's opening attention visualization and performance curve are replaced by a radar comparison and separate correlation plots. The framework diagram is extensively redrawn, Table 1 gains a denser structure with annotated differences, and qualitative comparisons expand to more methods and supplementary galleries. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for its mechanism and applicability through controlled correlation experiments (Figures 2 and 5), broader comparator coverage, specialized-domain evaluations (Table 9), and explicit runtime/memory analysis (Table 11). Branch ablations and discussion of alignment errors and computational limitations make the revised method easier to assess. Although some earlier parameter sweeps disappear and the method becomes more complex, the new evidence addresses important validation and practicality gaps in v1.
